title: How Much Fiber in Blackberries? 7.6g per Cup
description: Blackberries: about 7.6 g of fiber per 1 cup (27% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in blackberries?
intro: Blackberries rank #3 of 15 fruits on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in blackberries by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in blackberries?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists blackberries, raw at 5.3 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 cup; 144 g) therefore has about 7.6 g of fiber and 62 calories. That is 27% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 31% of a 25 g day and 20% of a 38 g day.
Blackberries are a close second to raspberries for fiber per cup among common berries. They are larger and juicier, so a cup holds fewer berries but weighs more.

sections.heading: Getting the most from blackberries
paragraphs: Like raspberries, blackberries are fragile and expensive out of season. Frozen blackberries are a good substitute for cooking and blending, and the fiber holds up.
Blackberry seeds are noticeable. If the texture bothers you in a smoothie, blend longer or mix with softer fruit like banana.

sections.heading: How blackberries compare with other fruits
paragraphs: Of the 15 fruits on this site, blackberries rank #3 for fiber per typical serving and #2 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 12.3 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [raspberries](/fiber-in-raspberries) at 8 g (1 cup); [pear](/fiber-in-pear) at 5.5 g (1 medium); [avocado](/fiber-in-avocado) at 10.1 g (1 medium avocado (flesh)). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), blackberries are #3 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding blackberries to your day
paragraphs: Mix blackberries with raspberries for a high-fiber berry bowl, or bake them into a crumble topped with oats.

Example: 1 cup blackberries, 1 cup oatmeal, 1 tbsp ground flaxseed. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 13.5 g of fiber, with 7.6 g from the blackberries. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of blackberries?
faqs.a: 5.3 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Blackberries, raw). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in blackberries (1/2 cup)?
faqs.a: About 3.8 g, for 72 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.
Yes. One cup gives a little over a quarter of the 28 g Daily Value, which is unusually high for fruit.
Raspberries edge ahead per cup: about 8 g (1 cup) versus about 7.6 g (1 cup). Either is a strong choice.
